source: Typical savings ranges compiled from US DOE / ENERGY STAR / ASHRAE efficiency-measure guidance — international benchmark ranges, not Singapore-metered results. Each range is the measure's saving as a % of the energy used by its own end-use category (e.g. a refrigeration measure's % is of refrigeration energy, not total electricity). Air-side economizers/free-cooling are intentionally excluded — not applicable to Singapore's tropical climate. `certainty` ("high" = hardware/capital measure with a fixed physical effect; "variable" = controls/software/behavioral measure whose realized saving depends on ongoing configuration and use, per site-visit feedback that BMS/setpoint-type savings are not guaranteed) and `effortTier` ("low"/"medium"/"high" implementation effort/disruption, distinct from cost) were added this phase to support ROI+effort-based ranking and honest confidence labeling — both are judgement calls made from the same evidence base, not separately re-sourced. Two chiller-plant measures (`high-efficiency-chiller-replacement`, `chiller-plant-optimization-controls`) were added 2026-09-24 to close a gap for commercial-building clients (Office/Professional Services, Retail, Hospitality, Healthcare) whose HVAC bill is chiller-plant-dominated — previously only fan/pump VSDs and generic BMS scheduling covered the HVAC end-use, with no measure addressing the chiller itself. Four more measures (`hvac-ec-fan-motor-retrofit`, `hvac-plant-room-ventilation`, `refrigeration-leak-detection-repair`, `refrigeration-low-gwp-transition`) were added 2026-09-26 from a client-supplied chiller/refrigeration ECM list, closing gaps in fan-motor hardware, plant-room heat rejection, and refrigerant-leak/transition measures. Onsite solar generation and RECs/EACs from that same list were deliberately NOT added here: they don't reduce an end-use's energy consumption the way every other catalog measure does (solar generates power, RECs/EACs are a market-based accounting claim), so scoring them against an end-use would either misstate or silently zero their impact — they're already modeled correctly elsewhere via the dedicated onsite-solar and renewable-coverage inputs in Scope 2.

measures.label: LED lighting retrofit
measures.evidence: US DOE — LED retrofits typically cut lighting energy 30-60% vs. fluorescent/incandescent baselines.
measures.howToImplement: Replace fluorescent/incandescent fixtures and tubes with LED equivalents during scheduled relamping or a single retrofit pass; most drop-in LED tubes/panels need no rewiring.

measures.label: Occupancy sensors & daylight harvesting controls
measures.evidence: US DOE — occupancy and daylight-linked lighting controls typically save a further 10-30% of lighting energy on top of the fixtures themselves.
measures.howToImplement: Install occupancy/PIR sensors and daylight-linked dimming ballasts on existing (or newly LED) fixtures, zoned by room usage pattern.

measures.label: Variable-speed drives on HVAC fans & pumps
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE — VSDs on HVAC fans and pumps typically cut that equipment's energy 20-50%, roughly 10-30% of total HVAC energy.
measures.howToImplement: Fit variable-speed drives to existing AHU/FCU fan and pump motors and commission them to modulate with actual load instead of running fixed-speed.

measures.label: BMS-based scheduling & setpoint optimization
measures.evidence: US DOE — BMS-based scheduling and setpoint optimization typically saves 5-15% of HVAC energy with no new capital equipment.
measures.howToImplement: Reprogram the existing BMS with occupancy-based schedules and optimized temperature setpoints — controls engineering time, no new hardware.

measures.label: High-efficiency chiller plant replacement
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE — replacing an aging constant-speed chiller plant with high-efficiency (VSD/magnetic-bearing) chillers typically cuts chiller energy 20-30%, the single largest lever in a commercial building's HVAC bill in a cooling-dominant climate like Singapore's.
measures.howToImplement: Replace the existing constant-speed chiller(s) with VSD/magnetic-bearing high-efficiency units at end-of-life or as a planned capital project; typically a multi-month procurement and installation.

measures.label: Chiller plant optimization (sequencing, condenser water reset)
measures.evidence: ASHRAE Guideline 36 / US DOE — optimized chiller sequencing and condenser water reset controls typically save 8-15% of HVAC energy without new chiller hardware; realized saving depends on ongoing commissioning and tuning, same caveat as other controls-only measures.
measures.howToImplement: Add or reprogram chiller sequencing and condenser-water-reset controls (e.g. per ASHRAE Guideline 36) on the existing chiller plant — a controls project, not new chiller hardware.

measures.label: High-efficiency EC/DC fan motor retrofit (rooftop units & condensers)
measures.evidence: US DOE / ENERGY STAR — replacing fixed-speed AC induction motors with electronically-commutated (EC/DC) motors on rooftop-unit and condenser fans typically cuts fan energy 15-30%, roughly 8-15% of total HVAC energy. Often installed as a hardware alternative or complement to a VSD retrofit on the same fans (see `hvac-vsd-fans-pumps`) rather than stacked for the full combined range.
measures.howToImplement: Swap fixed-speed AC motors on rooftop-unit and condenser fans for EC/DC motor equivalents during scheduled maintenance or motor failure replacement.

measures.label: Compressor / plant room ventilation & exhaust upgrade
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE mechanical-room guidance — inadequate ventilation and exhaust in a chiller/compressor plant room raises condensing temperature and derates compressor efficiency; ensuring adequate heat-rejection airflow typically recovers 3-8% of HVAC energy otherwise lost to this effect. Realized saving depends on ongoing airflow maintenance, not a one-off fix.
measures.howToImplement: Inspect and upgrade plant-room exhaust fans/louvres to ensure adequate airflow around chillers and compressors — usually a maintenance fix, occasionally a small capital upgrade.

measures.label: Refrigeration controls & floating head pressure
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE — floating head pressure and refrigeration controls typically cut refrigeration energy 8-15%.
measures.howToImplement: Add floating head pressure controls to existing refrigeration condensing units, tuned to ambient conditions instead of a fixed setpoint.

measures.label: Door strip curtains & open-door alarms on walk-in coolers
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — door strip curtains and open-door alarms typically save 3-6% of refrigeration energy by cutting infiltration.
measures.howToImplement: Fit strip curtains and door-open alarms to walk-in cooler/freezer doors — a low-disruption physical retrofit.

measures.label: Night covers on open refrigerated display cases
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR grocery guidance — night covers on open display cases typically save 2-5% of refrigeration energy.
measures.howToImplement: Fit night covers (manual or automated) to open refrigerated display cases, closed outside trading hours.

measures.label: High-efficiency refrigeration compressor replacement
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — replacing aging refrigeration compressors with high-efficiency units typically saves 10-20%.
measures.howToImplement: Replace aging refrigeration compressors with high-efficiency units at end-of-life or as a planned capital upgrade.

measures.label: Refrigerant leak detection & repair programme
measures.evidence: US DOE / ASHRAE — a refrigerant leak and the resulting undercharge forces the compressor to work harder to reach setpoint, typically wasting 5-10% of refrigeration energy in affected systems. A recurring maintenance action like `compressed-air-leak-survey` — savings depend on repeating the check, not a one-off fix. Repairing leaks also directly cuts Scope 1 fugitive refrigerant emissions, tracked separately via this tool's refrigerant GWP calculation (see `data/refrigerant_gwp.json`) — this ECM entry only covers the energy-saving side.
measures.howToImplement: Run a scheduled refrigerant leak-detection survey (ultrasonic/electronic detector) across refrigeration circuits and repair leaks found; repeat periodically as ongoing maintenance.

measures.label: Low-GWP refrigerant transition (ammonia / CO₂ systems)
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE industrial refrigeration guidance — ammonia (R-717) and CO₂ (R-744) systems typically run 10-20% more energy-efficient than an equivalent HFC system (e.g. R-410A, R-134a) at commercial/industrial scale, alongside a near-zero GWP versus R-410A's 2,088 (see `data/refrigerant_gwp.json`) — cuts both refrigeration energy and the Scope 1 fugitive-emissions intensity of any future leak. Major equipment replacement, not a retrofit.
measures.howToImplement: Replace existing HFC refrigeration equipment with ammonia or CO2-based systems at end-of-life or as a planned capital upgrade — new equipment, not a refrigerant swap in existing hardware.

measures.label: Demand-controlled kitchen exhaust hoods
measures.evidence: US DOE / ENERGY STAR — demand-controlled kitchen exhaust hoods typically cut associated fan energy 20-30%, roughly 10-20% of total cooking-area energy.
measures.howToImplement: Retrofit kitchen exhaust hoods with demand-controlled ventilation sensors that modulate fan speed to actual cooking load.

measures.label: ENERGY STAR certified cooking equipment
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — certified commercial fryers, griddles and ovens typically use 10-20% less energy than standard models.
measures.howToImplement: Replace fryers, griddles and ovens with ENERGY STAR-certified models at end-of-life or as a planned kitchen equipment refresh.

measures.label: Compressed air leak survey & repair
measures.evidence: US DOE — compressed air leak surveys and repair typically recover 5-10% of system energy (leaks commonly waste 20-30% before repair). Recurring maintenance action — savings depend on repeating the survey, not a one-off capital fix.
measures.howToImplement: Run a scheduled ultrasonic leak survey across the compressed air distribution system and repair leaks found; repeat periodically as ongoing maintenance.

measures.label: Variable-speed drives on process motors, pumps & fans
measures.evidence: US DOE — VSDs on motor-driven pumps, fans and compressors typically cut that equipment's energy 15-25%.
measures.howToImplement: Fit variable-speed drives to existing process motors, pumps and fans and commission them to modulate with actual load.

measures.label: Waste heat recovery on process equipment
measures.evidence: US DOE — waste heat recovery on industrial process equipment typically saves 5-12% of process energy.
measures.howToImplement: Install heat exchangers to capture waste heat from process equipment (exhaust, cooling water) and reuse it elsewhere in the facility — an engineering-led capital project.

measures.label: Laundry / drain-water heat recovery
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR hospitality guidance — drain-water and laundry heat recovery typically saves 10-20% of laundry energy.
measures.howToImplement: Install drain-water or laundry heat-recovery heat exchangers to preheat incoming water using outgoing hot water/drain heat.

measures.label: Low-flow fixtures & hot water system optimization
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — low-flow fixtures and hot water system optimization typically save 10-20% of hot water energy.
measures.howToImplement: Fit low-flow aerators/showerheads and optimize hot water system setpoints and recirculation scheduling — a low-disruption retrofit.

measures.label: Hot/cold aisle containment
measures.evidence: Huawei / Eaton data centre efficiency guidance — hot/cold aisle containment typically cuts cooling energy 10-25%.
measures.howToImplement: Install physical containment panels/curtains to separate hot and cold aisles in the data hall, directing cooling airflow more efficiently.

measures.label: High-efficiency UPS replacement
measures.evidence: Data centre efficiency guidance — replacing older UPS units with high-efficiency (>97%) models typically cuts UPS losses 20-40%.
measures.howToImplement: Replace older UPS units with high-efficiency (>97%) models at end-of-life or as a planned capital upgrade.

measures.label: Server virtualization & consolidation
measures.evidence: Common data centre efficiency practice — virtualization/consolidation typically cuts IT load energy 10-30% by raising utilization.
measures.howToImplement: Consolidate underutilized physical servers onto fewer, more heavily-utilized hosts via virtualization — an IT infrastructure project, not a facilities one.

measures.label: Dock door seals & loading-bay air curtains
measures.evidence: US DOE warehouse guidance — dock door seals and air curtains typically save 5-10% of material-handling-area energy via reduced infiltration.
measures.howToImplement: Fit dock door seals and loading-bay air curtains to reduce infiltration at loading bays — a low-disruption physical retrofit.

measures.label: Sterilizer / autoclave cycle batching & scheduling
measures.evidence: Healthcare energy management guidance — batching and scheduling sterilizer/autoclave cycles typically saves 5-10% of associated energy.
measures.howToImplement: Batch and schedule sterilizer/autoclave cycles to run fuller loads less often, coordinated with clinical/operational workflow.

measures.label: Plug load management (smart strips, PC power management)
measures.evidence: US DOE — plug load management typically saves 10-20% of plug load energy.
measures.howToImplement: Deploy smart power strips and enable PC power management settings across workstations — a low-cost IT/facilities rollout.

measures.label: Sub-metering & power-quality monitoring
measures.evidence: Cross-portfolio benchmark — sub-metering and power-quality monitoring typically surfaces 5-10% waste via anomaly detection by enabling further optimization, not by directly reducing load itself.
measures.howToImplement: Install sub-meters and power-quality monitoring at key distribution boards/circuits, then review the data for anomalies (equipment left running, phase imbalance).
